court: High Court of Judicature at Bombay
case_name: Manish Keshav Bediya And Ors vs The State Of Maharashtra And Anr

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Manish Keshav Bediya, Anita Keshav Bediya, Keshav Patoula Bediya, Nandini Keshav Bediya, Aarti Keshav Bediya (husband, wife, in-laws, unmarried sisters-in-law)
parties.respondent_defendant: The State of Maharashtra, Jyoti Manish Bediya (State, wife)

facts_of_case: Petitioners are husband and family members. Wife lodged FIR alleging offences under IPC sections 498-A, 323, 504 read with 34. Parties have amicably settled their dispute.

legal_principles.principle: Parties can settle their disputes amicably and seek quashing of the FIR.
legal_principles.held: The parties have amicably settled their dispute. Quashing is sought on the premise that the parties have amicably settled their dispute.

legal_principles.principle: Consent terms can be used to settle disputes and quash proceedings.
legal_principles.held: The parties decided to put up a quietus to the dispute and accordingly, entered into consent terms.

legal_principles.principle: Mutual consent can be used to dissolve a marriage.
legal_principles.held: The Family Court at Bandra has allowed the petition seeking divorce by mutual consent and has dissolved the marriage vide judgment and order dated 18th July, 2022.

outcome.final_order: Quashing of the FIR/complaint is sought and granted.

keywords: High Court of Judicature at Bombay
